newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Russian relief cosmonauts blast off to Mir.
newsitem.headline: Russian relief cosmonauts blast off to Mir.

text.p: A relief team of two Russian cosmonauts blasted off for the troubled Russian space station Mir at 1536 GMT on Tuesday.

Commander Anatoly Solovyov and flight engineer Pavel Vinogradov are expected to undertake the most vital repairs in the history of Mir, which collided with a resupply ship on June 25 and is running on partial power. The two cosmonauts are scheduled to arrive aboard on Thursday.

Mission Control outside Moscow broadcast live video of the two men, dressed in their spacesuits, as they blasted off into orbit. "In the first three minutes of flight everything is normal," a radio operator at Mission Control announced.
The Baikonur launch attracted an unusually high-ranking Russian delegation, including Defence Minister Igor Sergeyev and Yuri Baturin, secretary of President Boris Yeltsin's Defence Council.
Solovyov, 49, is a four-time veteran of the Mir space station who has spent a total of 456 days in space. Vinogradov, 43, is flying for the first time but will lead efforts to repair the ship.
The team is expected to don spacesuits on August 20 to reattach cables to the damaged Spektr module, an operation which, if successful, will restore power to much of the space station.
